trigger_condition: Web app imports from @price-tracker/shared but @price-tracker/shared is NOT listed as a dependency in apps/web/package.json. The transpilePackages setting in next.config.mjs references it, creating a phantom dependency.
guard_snippet: Add to apps/web/package.json dependencies: "@price-tracker/shared": "*"
potential_consequence: CRITICAL: npm workspace resolution currently works implicitly, but any non-Next.js consumer of this package, or a future migration to pnpm/yarn PnP, will fail to resolve @price-tracker/shared. Turbo's package graph also cannot detect this dependency, meaning turbo run build may not build shared before web.

trigger_condition: The $schema field is set to 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' which is the JSON Schema meta-specification, not the TypeScript configuration schema.
guard_snippet: Change $schema to: "https://json.schemastore.org/tsconfig"
potential_consequence: WARNING: IDEs (VS Code, WebStorm) that use the $schema field for IntelliSense will not provide tsconfig-specific autocompletion, validation, or hover docs. Developers will not get warnings for invalid compilerOptions keys.

trigger_condition: The 'main' and 'types' fields both point to './src/index.ts' (raw TypeScript source), while the build script runs 'tsc --build' outputting to './dist'. The dist output is never referenced.
guard_snippet: Either: (a) Add "exports" field: { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } } or (b) Change main to './dist/index.js' and types to './dist/index.d.ts' and keep source access via transpilePackages
potential_consequence: WARNING: The tsc --build step produces dist/ artifacts that nothing consumes. Any non-Next.js consumer (a CLI tool, a test runner, a future API server) importing @price-tracker/shared will receive raw .ts files which will fail to parse without a TypeScript loader. The build step is effectively dead code.

trigger_condition: The .dark block does not define --radius, while :root defines --radius: 0.5rem. If a future dark mode requires a different border radius (common in high-contrast dark themes), there is no override point.
guard_snippet: Add --radius: 0.5rem; to the .dark block to make it explicitly overridable
potential_consequence: LOW: Currently not a bug because the :root value cascades. But this is an incomplete dark mode token set -- every other variable has a dark override except --radius. A developer adding dark mode radius changes will have to discover this gap.

trigger_condition: The <html> element lacks suppressHydrationWarning={true}. When a dark mode toggle (next-themes or similar) is added later, it modifies the html class attribute on the client before hydration completes.
guard_snippet: <html lang="en" className={inter.variable} suppressHydrationWarning>
potential_consequence: WARNING: When dark mode toggling is implemented (the tailwind config already declares darkMode: ['class']), every page load will produce a React hydration mismatch warning in the console. The class-based dark mode infrastructure is half-built: the CSS variables and tailwind config are ready, but the layout lacks the hydration safety valve.

trigger_condition: The Toaster component is defined in src/components/ui/toaster.tsx and the use-toast hook exists, but neither is imported nor rendered anywhere in the component tree.
guard_snippet: Add to layout.tsx: import { Toaster } from '@/components/ui/toaster'; then render <Toaster /> inside <body> after {children}
potential_consequence: CRITICAL: Any call to toast() from use-toast.ts will update the in-memory state but nothing will render the toast UI. Toasts are completely invisible. This is dead code until Toaster is mounted in the layout.

trigger_condition: Tailwind content paths are ['./src/components/**/*.{ts,tsx}', './src/app/**/*.{ts,tsx}']. The paths omit ./src/lib/**, ./src/hooks/**, and any future ./src/pages/** or ./src/features/** directories.
guard_snippet: Change content to: ['./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'] to catch all source directories
potential_consequence: WARNING: Any Tailwind utility classes used in files under src/lib/ or src/hooks/ (or future directories like src/features/, src/layouts/) will be purged from the production CSS build. Currently src/lib/utils.ts and src/hooks/use-toast.ts do not use Tailwind classes, but this is a latent trap for future development.

trigger_condition: The plugins array uses require('tailwindcss-animate') which is CommonJS syntax inside a TypeScript file. Tailwind v3 handles this via jiti, but Tailwind v4 drops jiti and requires ESM imports.
guard_snippet: Change to: import tailwindcssAnimate from 'tailwindcss-animate'; then plugins: [tailwindcssAnimate]
potential_consequence: LOW: Not a current issue with Tailwind v3, but creates a migration blocker for Tailwind v4. The require() call will throw an ERR_REQUIRE_ESM error when upgrading.

trigger_condition: TOAST_REMOVE_DELAY is set to 1,000,000 milliseconds (16.7 minutes). Dismissed toasts remain in memory with active setTimeout handles for nearly 17 minutes before cleanup.
guard_snippet: Change to: const TOAST_REMOVE_DELAY = 5000; (5 seconds, or a reasonable UX delay)
potential_consequence: WARNING: In a dashboard application that shows frequent price alerts, rapid toast creation and dismissal will accumulate setTimeout handles and stale toast objects in memory. With TOAST_LIMIT=1, at most 1 toast renders, but dismissed toast objects and their timers persist for 16.7 minutes each.

trigger_condition: The useEffect dependency array includes [state], causing the listener to be unregistered and re-registered on every state change (every toast add/update/dismiss/remove).
guard_snippet: Change useEffect dependency to []: React.useEffect(() => { listeners.push(setState); return () => { const index = listeners.indexOf(setState); if (index > -1) listeners.splice(index, 1); }; }, []);
potential_consequence: WARNING: On every toast state change, the listener array is mutated (splice + push), causing unnecessary array reallocation. With frequent toasts this creates micro-GC pressure. The [state] dependency is unnecessary because setState identity is stable across renders.

trigger_condition: The shadcn/ui components.json aliases block only defines 'components' and 'utils'. It is missing 'ui', 'hooks', and 'lib' aliases.
guard_snippet: Add: "ui": "@/components/ui", "hooks": "@/hooks", "lib": "@/lib"
potential_consequence: WARNING: Running 'npx shadcn@latest add' for components that include hooks (like use-toast) will place files in incorrect locations or prompt for manual path input, because the CLI cannot resolve the hooks directory automatically.

trigger_condition: The universal selector * { @apply border-border; } applies border-color to every element in the DOM, including <html>, <head>, <meta>, <script>, and all non-visual elements.
guard_snippet: Consider scoping: *, *::before, *::after { border-color: hsl(var(--border)); } or use body * to exclude non-rendered elements (though this is standard shadcn/ui practice)
potential_consequence: LOW: Standard shadcn/ui pattern, but applies a CSS rule to every DOM element including ~50+ non-visual elements. Minor performance impact on initial style calculation for large DOMs. Not a functional bug.

trigger_condition: The .font-tabular class is defined outside any @layer directive. Tailwind utilities use @layer utilities which has lower specificity than unlayered styles.
guard_snippet: Move into: @layer utilities { .font-tabular { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } }
potential_consequence: WARNING: Because .font-tabular is unlayered, it cannot be overridden by Tailwind utility classes like tabular-nums or proportional-nums using the normal Tailwind specificity model. If both are applied, .font-tabular always wins regardless of class order.

trigger_condition: turbo.json does not define globalDependencies or globalEnv. Environment variables like NODE_ENV, NEXT_PUBLIC_*, or API keys do not invalidate the Turbo cache.
guard_snippet: Add: "globalDependencies": [".env"], "globalEnv": ["NODE_ENV", "NEXT_PUBLIC_*"]
potential_consequence: WARNING: Changing an environment variable (e.g., NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL) will not bust the Turbo cache. Developers will get stale builds with old env values. The 'FULL TURBO' cache hit means even adding a .env file later won't trigger rebuilds.

trigger_condition: noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters are set to true in the base tsconfig. These are inherited by the shared package which uses composite + tsc --build.
guard_snippet: Consider setting noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters to false in base and enabling them per-package, or add // @ts-ignore pragmas as needed
potential_consequence: LOW: Currently safe because shared/src/index.ts is trivial (export {}). But as shared grows, unused function parameters in type definitions, callback signatures, or interface implementations will cause tsc --build to fail. This is especially problematic with generated code or library type stubs.

trigger_condition: Web tsconfig inherits declaration: true and declarationMap: true from base, but also sets noEmit: true. The declaration/declarationMap settings are silently ignored when noEmit is true.
guard_snippet: No code change needed, but document that base tsconfig's declaration settings are overridden by web's noEmit: true
potential_consequence: LOW: Not a bug -- Next.js handles type checking separately. But it is confusing for developers reading the config: the effective compiler options differ from what the inheritance chain suggests. A developer might add a 'typecheck' script expecting .d.ts output and get none.

trigger_condition: packageManager field specifies npm@10.8.2 but no .nvmrc, .node-version, or .tool-versions file exists. The engines field requires node >= 18.17.0 but this is not enforced.
guard_snippet: Add .nvmrc with: 18.17.0 (or lts/hydrogen). Optionally add "engines": { "strict": true } or an .npmrc with engine-strict=true
potential_consequence: LOW: Without engine-strict, npm install succeeds on any Node version. A developer on Node 16 or 23 will get cryptic failures from Next.js 14 or TypeScript features. The packageManager field only works if corepack is enabled, which is not the default.

trigger_condition: The Dialog close button X icon is 16x16px (h-4 w-4) with no minimum touch target size. WCAG 2.5.8 (Target Size minimum) requires interactive elements to be at least 24x24px.
guard_snippet: Add padding or min size to the close button: className="... min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] flex items-center justify-center"
potential_consequence: LOW: On touch devices, the small close button (16x16 visible area within a roughly 24x24 clickable area due to padding) may be difficult to tap accurately. The absolute positioning with right-4 top-4 provides some implicit padding, but the actual interactive element is small.

trigger_condition: The Input component uses ring-offset-background utility class which references Tailwind's ring-offset-color. This requires the CSS variable --background to be available, which it is via globals.css, but the ring-offset-color is not explicitly configured in tailwind.config.ts.
guard_snippet: This works because Tailwind's ring-offset utility with arbitrary values: ring-offset-background resolves via the configured 'background' color token. No change needed, but add a comment for clarity.
potential_consequence: LOW: Works correctly because 'background' is defined as a Tailwind color token. If the 'background' color key were ever renamed or removed from the Tailwind config, the ring-offset would silently fall back to transparent.

trigger_condition: Root package.json uses npm workspaces with glob patterns 'apps/*' and 'packages/*'. If a non-package directory (e.g., apps/docs, packages/config) is added without a package.json, npm install will fail.
guard_snippet: Use explicit workspace paths instead of globs if the project structure is stable, or document the workspace convention
potential_consequence: LOW: Standard monorepo pattern, but any directory accidentally created under apps/ or packages/ without a package.json will cause npm install to error with 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, open .../package.json'.

trigger_condition: No test script or test framework (jest, vitest, @testing-library) is configured in the web app. The Turbo pipeline does not include a 'test' task.
guard_snippet: Add vitest + @testing-library/react to devDependencies. Add "test": "vitest run" to scripts. Add test task to turbo.json.
potential_consequence: WARNING: There is no automated testing infrastructure. UI components (Button, Dialog, Toast, Table, Input) ship with zero test coverage. Regressions from future shadcn/ui component updates or Tailwind config changes will not be caught.

trigger_condition: eslint-config-next is pinned to ^14.2.29 while the resolved eslint-config-next version is 14.2.35 (matching the resolved next version). But eslint is pinned to ^8.57.1, and eslint-config-next ^14 only supports eslint ^7.23.0 || ^8.0.0. ESLint 9.x is the current major release.
guard_snippet: Document that ESLint 9 migration requires eslint-config-next 15+ and Next.js 15
potential_consequence: LOW: Not broken today, but the ESLint 8 + eslint-config-next 14 combination is a dead end. ESLint 8 is in maintenance mode. When upgrading to ESLint 9, the flat config format is required, the .eslintrc.json format is deprecated, and eslint-config-next must be upgraded to v15+ simultaneously.
